key_insight: A missing streamwise-gradient term in the normal diffusive flux causes a bulk-surface mass imbalance in soluble-surfactant falling-film models; adding it restores exact conservation without changing the hydrodynamics or linear stability.
engineering_relevance: For reduced-order film-surfactant solvers, this correction is essential to guarantee physically consistent mass budgets in long-time simulations and design studies.
method: Audited nonlinear weighted-residual bulk-surface transport equations for conservation errors
Derived the mass imbalance analytically and constructed periodic concentration fields that expose it
Added the omitted flux contribution and checked that conservation is restored while the base dynamics remain unchanged
evidence_signal: In a no-slip benchmark, the reference model lost 0.0228832% of initial surfactant mass by t=4500, while the corrected model showed an absolute relative mass change of 1.2×10^-15.
watch_item: The correction preserves reduced-model conservation, but it does not by itself ensure full compatibility with higher-order curved-interface boundary conditions.
paper_title: A conservative bulk-surface closure for soluble-surfactant falling films: an analytical and numerical mass-balance audit
